messages:
devon: FYI onboarding run for orca-v1.3 hit two separate problems in staging this morning: a tokenizer mismatch that produced garbled completions and an OOM while trying to load the 8-bit quant weights.

maria: ugh. which weights path did we use? was this the new s3 artifact from the CI bundle?

devon: s3://redwood-models/orca-v1.3/weights.tar.gz (artifact was built by circle job #4521). tokenizer files were in the tar but size/filenames looked off.

alex: can you paste the tokenizer error? quick glance might tell if it's vocab/order mismatch.

devon: error from the python loader: 
```
ValueError: Tokenizer files do not match model config. expected tokens=50257 found=50255 (tokenizer mismatch)
```
Outputs were like: "<|unk|> Hello how many????" for normal prompts.

samir: that token count delta smells like a truncated merges/vocab. maybe the tar step dropped tokenizer.json. I saw a similar CI bug when parallel uploads raced.

jin: I pulled the tar locally and ran `python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; print(Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer.json').token_to_id('[UNK]'))"` — it fails, file is 0 bytes in the artifact. looks like the pack step wrote a placeholder.

devon: confirmed. CI job log shows `aws s3 cp tokenizer.json s3://...` returned 0 exit but we still continued. attaching snippet from circle: `Uploading artifacts... 0 bytes uploaded for tokenizer.json`

infra-bot: deploy-check: staging cluster reported memory pressure during model load at 2026-03-15T09:12:30Z. Node g4-3 had RSS spike to 63GB then OOM-kill on process pid 7321.

maria: for the OOM, was this during full model load or when quantizing on the host? we should avoid host-side quant steps.

devon: we attempted fallback quantization (8-bit) on the runtime because the artifact lacked proper 8-bit weights. That put a spike in CPU/RAM.

alex: immediate mitigation: rollback to orca-v1.2 artifact and mark v1.3 artifacts invalid in the model catalog. can someone run `redwoodctl models set-default orca v1.2 --env staging`?

samir: I'm on it. will also add a check in the CI pack pipeline to fail if tokenizer.json size < 1KB.

jin: short-term hotfix: re-run pack job with explicit `--include tokenizer.json` and verify `sha256sum` matches. I'll open a tiny PR to the packer in ~15m.

devon: thanks. long-term action items: (1) CI: assert tokenizer and weights sizes + token count match model config, (2) runtime: refuse to fallback to host-side quant if artifact claims quantized weights are present, (3) add a canary step that runs a sanity prompt and checks tokenization/response for new artifacts before promoting.

maria: please create issues and tag oncall/eng-ml. Also add a quick alert: artifact-validator failure should page on-call if token count mismatch occurs.

ops-bot: issue created: #ML-848 "Artifact packer: fail on missing tokenizer or size mismatch" assigned to @samir.

samir: created PR for CI size check: https://git.internal/redwood/pack/pull/67 (WIP). will add token-count assert after jin's checksum fix.

alex: devon, once we rollback and confirm staging prompts look good, can you post a short playback of 3 sample prompts (one instruction, one chat, one long-context) so we have a regression artifact?

devon: will do after rollback. rolling back now and will post results + logs. :thumbsup:

jin: also adding a unit test in tokenizers/ that loads tokenizer.json and asserts `vocab_size == expected` and `contains('[UNK]')`. should reduce silent packaging regressions.

devon: final note: if anyone hits similar issues in prod, don't trigger runtime-side quantize. escalate and we'll rollback to last-good artifact.

maria: thanks all — nice triage. follow-ups in #ML-848 and I'll schedule a 15-min sync tomorrow to make sure the canary workflow is defined. :calendar:
